Whether each visit is in under one rule, on the stream branch

Source: R/rule_in.R
knw_rule_in.Rd

scripts/0297's rule: a visit on a stream edge is in when its gradient lies in [0, grad_max] and either the size test holds (width in [size_min, 9999], or MAD at least size_min) or the exception does (a river of at least exc_q m³/s within exc_d m downstream on the flow source src). A NA gradient, width or MAD fails its test. The river, wetland and lake branches of link's rules are constant across the rules a grid varies, so a scoring population holds stream-branch visits only, and a visit off the stream edges is out here.

Usage

knw_rule_in(
  d,
  rule,
  walks = NULL,
  cols = c(grad = "fwa_gradient", width = "cw_deploy", mad = "mad_pick"),
  src = "pick",
  edge_stream = c(1000L, 1100L, 2000L, 2300L),
  no_lake_target = FALSE,
  no_reg_target = FALSE
)

Arguments

d

data.frame of visits with edge_type, blue_line_key, downstream_route_measure and the columns named by cols.

rule

one row of knw_tune_grid()'s table.

walks

the index knw_walk_index() returns, or NULL when no rule in play has an exception.

cols

named character: which columns of d carry grad, width and mad.

src

character(1) the flow source the exception reads.

edge_stream

integer the stream-branch edge types.

no_lake_target, no_reg_target

logical(1) fail the exception where the river found is a lake segment, or lies on a regulated reach.

Value

logical of nrow(d).

Examples

d <- data.frame(edge_type = c(1000, 1000, 1250), blue_line_key = 1, downstream_route_measure = 1:3,
                fwa_gradient = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.01), cw_deploy = c(2, 1, 50), mad_pick = c(0.3, 0.1, 40))
r <- data.frame(size_var = "width", size_min = 1.5, grad_max = 0.0549, exc_q = NA, exc_d = NA)
knw_rule_in(d, r)
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE FALSE
